options.B: Sinkhole

questions.explanation: Sinkholes are characteristic of karst terrain formed by groundwater solution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A natural levee forms due to:

options.A: Wind abrasion
options.B: Overbank river deposition

questions.explanation: Floodwater deposits coarser sediment near channel banks, forming a natural levee.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are interlocking spurs?

options.A: Depositional features on the inner bends of meanders
options.B: Erosional landforms in the upper course where alternate valley sides project into the valley, interlocking with each other
options.C: Ridges of glacial debris along valley sides

questions.explanation: Interlocking spurs are landforms produced by river erosion, common in the upper course where the river winds around alternating projections of valley sides.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are incised meanders?

options.A: Meanders formed by deposition in a floodplain
options.B: Meanders that have been cut deeply into bedrock by renewed vertical erosion

questions.explanation: Incised meanders are a river erosion landform where meanders are deeply cut into bedrock, often due to rejuvenation or uplift.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a river cliff or cut bank?

options.A: A depositional feature on the inner bend of a meander
options.B: A steep bank formed by lateral erosion on the outer bend of a meander
options.C: A ridge of debris along a glacier
options.D: A cliff formed by wave action

questions.explanation: River cliffs or cut banks are erosional features on the outer bends of meanders where lateral erosion is strongest. Point bars form on the inner bends.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are rapids?

options.A: Sections of a river where the gradient is steep and the water flows quickly over resistant rocks or boulders
options.B: Depositional features at a river mouth

questions.explanation: Rapids are sections of a river with steep gradient and turbulent flow over resistant rocks or boulders, and are a river erosion landform.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea cave?

options.A: A vertical opening connected to a sea cave through which air and water are forced upwards
options.B: A hollow eroded into a cliff by wave action, especially where waves enlarge weaknesses and joints
options.C: A narrow steep-sided inlet cut into a rocky coast
options.D: A gently sloping rocky platform left by cliff retreat

questions.explanation: A sea cave is a hollow eroded into a cliff by wave action where waves enlarge weaknesses and joints. It may later cut through a headland to form an arch.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea arch?

options.A: A cave that has cut through a headland, leaving a bridge of rock with an opening beneath
options.B: A vertical opening connected to a sea cave
options.C: A narrow steep-sided inlet cut into a rocky coast

questions.explanation: A sea arch forms when a cave cuts through a headland. Collapse of the arch roof may leave a stack.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea stack?

options.A: A cave that has cut through a headland
options.B: An isolated pillar of rock left standing offshore after the collapse of a sea arch
options.C: A narrow steep-sided inlet cut into a rocky coast

questions.explanation: A sea stack is an isolated pillar of rock left offshore after the collapse of a sea arch. Continued erosion and collapse reduce it to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea stump?

options.A: An isolated pillar of rock offshore
options.B: The remnant of a sea stack after continued erosion and collapse, often submerged at high tide
options.C: A cave cutting through a headland

questions.explanation: A sea stump is the remnant of a sea stack after continued erosion and collapse. It is often submerged at high tide.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an erosional desert landform?

options.A: Barchan dune
options.B: Loess deposit

questions.explanation: Yardangs are erosional desert landforms carved by wind abrasion and deflation. Barchan dunes, transverse dunes and loess are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an erosional glacial landform?

options.A: Esker
options.B: Kame

questions.explanation: A cirque is an erosional glacial landform. Esker, kame and outwash plain are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional glacial landform?

options.A: Arête
options.B: Horn

questions.explanation: A drumlin is an elongated hill of glacial sediment and is depositional. Arête, horn and U-shaped valley are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional coastal landform?

options.A: Sea cave
options.B: Sea arch

questions.explanation: A spit is a depositional coastal landform formed by longshore drift. Sea cave, sea arch and wave-cut notch are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a groundwater erosion landform?

options.A: Barchan dune
options.B: Sinkhole

questions.explanation: Sinkholes are karst landforms formed by groundwater solution. Barchan dune is wind depositional, esker is glacial depositional, and spit is marine depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a form of solution/corrosion?

options.A: The force of water pressure loosening material
options.B: Chemical dissolution of soluble rock by water

questions.explanation: Solution or corrosion is the chemical dissolution of soluble minerals and rocks by water, especially weakly acidic water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which process deepens a plunge pool at the base of a waterfall?

options.A: Deflation
options.B: Hydraulic action and abrasion

questions.explanation: Hydraulic action and abrasion deepen a plunge pool and undercut the resistant ledge at a waterfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial landform is formed when several cirques erode back towards one another?

options.A: Arête
options.B: Horn

questions.explanation: A horn is a sharp, pyramidal mountain peak formed when several cirques erode back towards one another. An arête forms between adjacent cirques or glacially eroded valleys.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Why may waterfalls occur at the outlet of a hanging valley?

options.A: Because the hanging valley is at a lower level than the main trough
options.B: Because the hanging valley is left at a higher level than the main glacial trough, and water drops down to the main valley
options.C: Because the hanging valley is formed by wind erosion
options.D: Because the hanging valley is a depositional feature

questions.explanation: A hanging valley is a tributary glacial valley left at a higher level than the main glacial trough because the main glacier eroded more deeply. Waterfalls may occur at its outlet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an important form of hydraulic action on a coast?

options.A: Wave quarrying and pressure in joints
options.B: Deflation and abrasion

questions.explanation: Wave quarrying and pressure in joints are important forms of hydraulic action in marine erosion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which acid is formed when rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and soil?

options.A: Sulphuric acid
options.B: Carbonic acid

questions.explanation: Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and soil, forming weak carbonic acid, which dissolves calcite in limestone.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following deposits is typically well-sorted?

options.A: Glacial till
options.B: Wind-blown sand

questions.explanation: Wind and waves often produce well-sorted deposits. Glacial till is typically poorly sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following deposits is typically poorly sorted?

options.A: Wind-blown sand
options.B: Wave-deposited beach sand

questions.explanation: Glacial till is typically poorly sorted because it is deposited directly by ice without the sorting action of water or wind. Outwash is stratified and better sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Where is deposition common in a river system?

options.A: On outer meander bends and steep upper courses
options.B: On inner meander bends, floodplains, river mouths and where gradient decreases

questions.explanation: River deposition is common on inner meander bends, floodplains, river mouths and where gradient decreases.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What controls delta development at a river mouth?

options.A: Only the river's length
options.B: Sediment supply, waves, tides and currents

questions.explanation: Delta development depends on sediment supply, waves, tides and currents. Delta formation is not automatic at every river mouth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the classic example of a loess deposit?

options.A: Sahara Desert
options.B: Loess Plateau of China

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau of China is a classic example of loess, a widespread deposit of wind-blown silt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial deposit is stratified and better sorted?

options.A: Till
options.B: Ground moraine

questions.explanation: Outwash is deposited by meltwater and is usually stratified and better sorted, unlike till which is deposited directly by ice and is unsorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the main process responsible for the formation of a spit?

options.A: Glacial plucking
options.B: Longshore drift

questions.explanation: A spit is commonly formed by longshore drift, which transports sediment along the coast and deposits it where the coastline changes direction or the flow energy decreases.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following connects an island to the mainland or to another island?

options.A: Spit
options.B: Bar

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a ridge or bar of sediment connecting an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef?

options.A: Fjord
options.B: Coastal lagoon

questions.explanation: A coastal lagoon is a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef, with a restricted connection to the open sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rocks are commonly associated with karst landscapes?

options.A: Granite and basalt
options.B: Limestone, dolomite and gypsum

questions.explanation: Karst landscapes develop mainly by solution of soluble rocks such as limestone, dolomite or gypsum.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the main difference between a waterfall and rapids?

options.A: A waterfall is a vertical drop; rapids are turbulent, fast-flowing sections over resistant rocks or boulders without a single vertical drop
options.B: A waterfall is formed by wind; rapids by water
options.C: A waterfall is depositional; rapids are erosional
options.D: A waterfall forms in the lower course; rapids form in the upper course

questions.explanation: A waterfall involves a vertical drop where differential erosion creates a step. Rapids are turbulent, fast-flowing sections over resistant rocks or boulders, without necessarily a single vertical drop.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between a drumlin and an esker?

options.A: A drumlin is a winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel; an esker is an elongated hill of till
options.B: A drumlin is an elongated streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment; an esker is a long winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater
options.D: Both are formed by wind deposition

questions.explanation: A drumlin is an elongated, streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment. An esker is a long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which dune type forms where winds blow from multiple directions?

options.A: Barchan
options.B: Parabolic

questions.explanation: A star dune is a high, pyramidal dune with several arms, formed where winds blow from multiple directions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Arrange the coastal erosional features in the correct sequence of formation from a cave.

options.A: Cave → stack → arch → stump
options.B: Cave → arch → stack → stump

questions.explanation: Waves enlarge weaknesses and joints to form caves. A cave may cut through a headland to form an arch. Collapse of the arch roof leaves a stack; continued erosion and collapse reduce it to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between an alluvial fan and a delta?

options.A: An alluvial fan forms where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain; a delta forms at a river mouth where the river enters standing water
options.B: An alluvial fan forms at a river mouth; a delta forms at the foot of a mountain
options.C: Both form only in glacial environments

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan is a fan-shaped deposit formed where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain. A delta is a depositional landform at a river mouth where sediment accumulates as the river enters standing water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between a deflation hollow and a desert pavement?

options.A: A deflation hollow is a depression formed by wind removing loose material; a desert pavement is a surface layer of closely packed pebbles left behind after wind removes finer particles
options.B: A deflation hollow is a surface layer of pebbles; a desert pavement is a depression
options.D: Both are formed by glacial action

questions.explanation: A deflation hollow or blowout is a depression formed when wind removes loose surface material. A desert pavement is a surface layer of closely packed pebbles and gravel left behind after wind removes finer particles by deflation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a glacial erosional landform?

options.A: Cirque
options.B: Arête

questions.explanation: A drumlin is a depositional glacial landform composed mainly of glacial sediment. Cirque, arête and hanging valley are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional feature in karst landscapes?

options.A: Sinkhole
options.B: Swallow hole

questions.explanation: Stalactites (and stalagmites) are depositional cave formations produced by precipitation of calcite from solution. Sinkholes, swallow holes and dolines are erosional or collapse features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform produced by river erosion?

options.A: Point bar
options.B: Natural levee

questions.explanation: Incised meanders are a river erosion landform. Point bars, natural levees and alluvial fans are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform produced by river deposition?

options.A: V-shaped valley
options.B: Gorge

questions.explanation: Point bars are depositional features on the inner bends of meanders. V-shaped valleys, gorges and waterfalls are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a wind depositional landform?

options.A: Yardang
options.B: Ventifact

questions.explanation: Loess is a wind depositional landform. Yardang, ventifact and deflation hollow are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a wind erosional landform?

options.A: Barchan dune
options.B: Loess

questions.explanation: Ventifacts are rocks faceted, polished or grooved by wind-blown sand and are erosional features. Barchan dunes, loess and parabolic dunes are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a glacial erosional feature found between adjacent cirques?

options.A: Horn
options.B: Arête

questions.explanation: An arête is a narrow, sharp-edged ridge formed between adjacent glacial cirques or glacially eroded valleys. A horn forms where several cirques erode back towards one another.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a long, narrow coastal deposit lying offshore and roughly parallel to the coast?

options.A: Spit
options.B: Tombolo

questions.explanation: A barrier beach or barrier island is a long, narrow coastal deposit of sand or shingle lying offshore and roughly parallel to the coast, separated from the mainland by a lagoon or tidal waterway.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a network of shallow, interconnecting channels separated by sediment bars?

options.A: Meander
options.B: Braided channel

questions.explanation: Braided channels are a network of shallow, interconnecting channels separated by temporary or persistent sediment bars, often associated with abundant sediment load and variable discharge.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: An oxbow lake is formed when:

options.A: A meander loop is cut off from the main channel, and deposition may seal the abandoned loop
options.B: A glacier plucks bedrock
options.D: A bar connects an island to the mainland

questions.explanation: An oxbow lake forms when a meander loop is cut off from the main channel. Erosion narrows the meander neck; deposition may seal the abandoned loop, leaving a crescent-shaped lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which moraine marks the maximum extent of a glacier during an advance?

options.A: Lateral moraine
options.B: Medial moraine

questions.explanation: A terminal or end moraine is a ridge of debris deposited at or near the farthest advance of a glacier, marking its maximum extent during that advance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which moraine forms where the lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join?

options.A: Lateral moraine
options.B: Medial moraine

questions.explanation: A medial moraine is a debris ridge near the centre of a glacier, commonly formed where lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which moraine is deposited during a temporary pause or minor readvance as a glacier retreats?

options.A: Terminal moraine
options.B: Recessional moraine

questions.explanation: A recessional moraine is a ridge deposited during a temporary pause or minor readvance as a glacier retreats.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial deposit is a widespread, often gently undulating layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice?

options.A: Ground moraine
options.B: Terminal moraine

questions.explanation: A ground moraine is a widespread, often gently undulating layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is formed by waves enlarging weaknesses and joints in a cliff?

options.A: Sea cave
options.B: Sea stack

questions.explanation: Sea caves form when waves enlarge weaknesses and joints in a cliff. A cave may later cut through a headland to form an arch.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is formed by the collapse of a sea arch roof?

options.A: Sea cave
options.B: Sea stack

questions.explanation: Collapse of the arch roof leaves a stack. Continued erosion and collapse reduce it to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a narrow, steep-sided inlet or cleft cut into a rocky coast along a structural weakness?

options.A: Blowhole
options.B: Geo

questions.explanation: A geo or geos is a narrow, steep-sided inlet or cleft cut into a rocky coast, commonly by marine erosion along a structural weakness.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a closed depression in karst terrain formed by dissolution, collapse of a cave roof or gradual subsidence?

options.A: Swallow hole
options.B: Sinkhole/doline

questions.explanation: A sinkhole or doline is a closed depression in karst terrain formed by dissolution, collapse of a cave roof or gradual subsidence into underground openings.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an opening through which a surface stream disappears underground?

options.A: Sinkhole
options.B: Doline

questions.explanation: A swallow hole is an opening through which a surface stream disappears underground into a cave or subterranean drainage system.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which cave formation hangs from the ceiling?

options.A: Stalagmite
options.B: Stalactite

questions.explanation: Stalactites hang from cave ceilings; stalagmites grow upward from cave floors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which cave formation grows upward from the cave floor?

options.A: Stalactite
options.B: Stalagmite

questions.explanation: Stalagmites grow upward from cave floors; stalactites hang from cave ceilings.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which mode of transport carries dissolved ions and minerals in water?

options.A: Traction
options.B: Saltation

questions.explanation: Solution load consists of dissolved ions and minerals carried in water. They are transported in dissolved form and are not visible as solid sediment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which mode of transport carries fine particles such as silt and clay within a moving fluid by turbulence?

options.A: Traction
options.B: Saltation

questions.explanation: Suspension occurs when fine particles such as silt and clay are held within a moving fluid by turbulence and carried over considerable distances.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which mode of transport moves coarse particles by rolling, sliding or dragging along the bed?

options.A: Traction
options.B: Saltation

questions.explanation: Traction is the rolling, sliding or dragging of larger particles along the bed by flowing water or wind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which mode of transport involves short hops or bounces of sand-sized particles?

options.A: Traction
options.B: Saltation

questions.explanation: Saltation is a bouncing or hopping movement of sand-sized or small gravel particles along a surface, commonly used to describe transport by rivers and wind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How are sediments transported by glaciers?

options.A: Only by suspension
options.B: Supraglacially, englacially and subglacially

questions.explanation: Glaciers carry debris on their surface (supraglacial), within the ice (englacial) and at the base (subglacial). They can transport particles from clay-sized material to very large boulders.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a mode of wind transport?

options.A: Suspension
options.B: Saltation

questions.explanation: Wind transports particles mainly by suspension, saltation and surface creep (traction). Solution is not a significant mode of wind transport.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is longshore drift?

options.A: The movement of sediment along a coast when waves approach at an angle and swash carries material obliquely up the beach while backwash returns it downslope
options.B: The movement of sediment directly offshore by backwash
options.C: The deposition of sediment at a river mouth
options.D: The transport of sediment by wind along a beach

questions.explanation: Longshore drift is the movement of sediment along a coast when waves approach the shore at an angle and swash carries material obliquely up the beach while backwash returns it downslope under gravity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is competence in sediment transport?

options.A: The total quantity of sediment a transporting agent can carry
options.B: The maximum particle size that a transporting agent can move under given conditions
options.C: The degree to which sediment particles are similar in size
options.D: The smoothing of particle edges during transport

questions.explanation: Competence is the maximum particle size that a transporting agent can move under given conditions. Faster or more energetic flow generally has greater competence.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is capacity in sediment transport?

options.A: The maximum particle size a transporting agent can move
options.B: The total quantity of sediment a transporting agent can carry under given conditions
options.C: The degree to which sediment particles are similar in size
options.D: The smoothing of particle edges during transport

questions.explanation: Capacity is the total quantity of sediment a transporting agent can carry under given conditions. It depends strongly on energy, discharge and turbulence.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a graded deposit?

options.A: A deposit in which particles show sorting by size or density, often with coarser material deposited before finer material as energy decreases
options.B: A deposit in which all particles are the same size
options.C: A deposit formed directly by glacial ice
options.D: A deposit formed by chemical precipitation

questions.explanation: A graded deposit is a sediment deposit in which particles show sorting by size or density, often with coarser material deposited before finer material as energy decreases.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is sorting?

options.A: The smoothing of particle edges during transport
options.B: The degree to which sediment particles are similar in size; wind and waves often produce well-sorted deposits, while glacial till is typically poorly sorted
options.C: The maximum particle size a transporting agent can move
options.D: The total quantity of sediment a transporting agent can carry

questions.explanation: Sorting is the degree to which sediment particles are similar in size. Wind and waves often produce well-sorted deposits; glacial till is typically poorly sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is rounding?

options.A: The sorting of particles by size
options.B: The smoothing of particle edges during transport by abrasion and collisions
options.C: The maximum particle size a transporting agent can move
options.D: The total quantity of sediment a transporting agent can carry

questions.explanation: Rounding is the smoothing of particle edges during transport by abrasion and collisions. Longer or more energetic transport often increases rounding, although rock type and transport conditions matter.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is an alluvial fan?

options.A: A fan-shaped deposit of gravel, sand and finer alluvium formed where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain
options.B: A ridge of sediment deposited along a river bank during floods
options.C: A depositional landform at a river mouth
options.D: A crescent-shaped lake formed from a meander

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan is a fan-shaped deposit of gravel, sand and finer alluvium formed where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain, loses velocity and spreads out.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a floodplain?

options.A: A fan-shaped deposit at the foot of a mountain
options.B: A relatively flat area alongside a river built by repeated overbank deposition and channel migration during floods
options.C: A ridge of sand and gravel on the inner side of a meander
options.D: A depositional landform at a river mouth

questions.explanation: A floodplain is a relatively flat area alongside a river built by repeated overbank deposition and channel migration during floods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are natural levees?

options.A: Raised embankments of relatively coarse sediment deposited along river banks when floodwater spills out of the channel, loses velocity and drops its heavier load near the banks
options.B: Ridges of sand and gravel deposited on the inner side of a meander
options.C: Fan-shaped deposits at the foot of mountains

questions.explanation: Natural levees are raised embankments of relatively coarse sediment deposited along river banks when floodwater spills out of the channel, loses velocity and drops its heavier load near the banks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a point bar?

options.A: A raised embankment along a river bank
options.B: A deposit of sand and gravel on the inner, slower-flowing side of a meander bend where river velocity is lower
options.C: A fan-shaped deposit at the foot of a mountain
options.D: A depositional landform at a river mouth

questions.explanation: A point bar is a deposit of sand and gravel on the inner, slower-flowing side of a meander bend where river velocity is lower.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a delta?

options.A: A fan-shaped deposit at the foot of a mountain
options.B: A depositional landform at a river mouth where sediment accumulates as the river enters a standing body of water and loses velocity
options.C: A ridge of sand attached to land at one end
options.D: A crescent-shaped lake formed from a meander

questions.explanation: A delta is a depositional landform at a river mouth where sediment accumulates as the river enters a standing body of water and loses velocity. Delta development depends on sediment supply, waves, tides and currents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are braided channels?

options.A: A single deep channel with a meandering course
options.B: A network of shallow, interconnecting channels separated by temporary or persistent sediment bars, often associated with abundant sediment load and variable discharge
options.C: A channel cut into resistant rock
options.D: A channel formed by glacial meltwater beneath ice

questions.explanation: Braided channels are a network of shallow, interconnecting channels separated by temporary or persistent sediment bars, often associated with abundant sediment load and variable discharge.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is an oxbow lake and is it depositional?

options.A: An oxbow lake forms when a meander loop is cut off from the main channel; erosion narrows the meander neck, and deposition may seal the abandoned loop, leaving a crescent-shaped lake
options.B: An oxbow lake is formed by glacial plucking and is purely erosional
options.C: An oxbow lake is formed by wind deflation and is purely erosional
options.D: An oxbow lake is formed by wave erosion and is purely erosional

questions.explanation: An oxbow lake forms when a meander loop is cut off from the main channel. Erosion narrows the meander neck; deposition may seal the abandoned loop, leaving a crescent-shaped lake.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: When does wind deposit sediment?

options.A: When wind velocity or turbulence increases
options.B: When wind velocity or turbulence decreases, or when obstacles, vegetation, moisture or surface conditions reduce its ability to transport particles
options.C: When the wind direction changes to blow uphill
options.D: When the wind carries only dissolved material

questions.explanation: Wind deposits sediment when wind velocity or turbulence decreases, or when obstacles, vegetation, moisture or surface conditions reduce its ability to transport particles.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are sand dunes?

options.A: Depressions formed by wind deflation
options.B: Mounds or ridges of wind-deposited sand whose shape depends on wind direction and variability, sand supply, vegetation and surface conditions
options.D: Long streamlined ridges carved by wind

questions.explanation: Sand dunes are mounds or ridges of wind-deposited sand. Their shape depends on wind direction and variability, sand supply, vegetation and surface conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a barchan dune?

options.A: A crescent-shaped dune formed where sand supply is limited and wind direction is relatively constant; its horns point downwind
options.B: A U-shaped dune stabilised by vegetation with arms pointing upwind
options.C: A long narrow ridge aligned parallel to the prevailing wind
options.D: A high pyramidal dune with several arms

questions.explanation: A barchan dune is a crescent-shaped dune formed where sand supply is limited and wind direction is relatively constant. Its horns point downwind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a transverse dune?

options.A: A crescent-shaped dune with horns pointing downwind
options.B: A ridge of sand oriented broadly at right angles to the prevailing wind, generally formed where sand supply is abundant and wind direction is fairly consistent
options.C: A long ridge aligned parallel to the prevailing wind
options.D: A U-shaped dune with arms pointing upwind

questions.explanation: A transverse dune is a ridge of sand oriented broadly at right angles to the prevailing wind, generally formed where sand supply is abundant and wind direction is fairly consistent.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a longitudinal or seif dune?

options.A: A crescent-shaped dune with horns pointing downwind
options.B: A ridge of sand oriented at right angles to the prevailing wind
options.C: A long, narrow ridge generally aligned parallel or nearly parallel to the resultant prevailing wind direction, often associated with more than one effective wind direction
options.D: A U-shaped dune stabilised by vegetation

questions.explanation: A longitudinal or seif dune is a long, narrow ridge generally aligned parallel or nearly parallel to the resultant prevailing wind direction, often associated with more than one effective wind direction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a parabolic dune?

options.A: A crescent-shaped dune with horns pointing downwind
options.B: A U-shaped dune commonly stabilised by vegetation; its arms point upwind, opposite to the horns of a barchan
options.C: A long ridge aligned parallel to the prevailing wind
options.D: A high pyramidal dune with several arms

questions.explanation: A parabolic dune is a U-shaped dune commonly stabilised by vegetation; its arms point upwind, opposite to the horns of a barchan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a star dune?

options.A: A crescent-shaped dune with horns pointing downwind
options.B: A U-shaped dune with arms pointing upwind
options.C: A high, pyramidal dune with several arms, formed where winds blow from multiple directions
options.D: A long ridge aligned parallel to the prevailing wind

questions.explanation: A star dune is a high, pyramidal dune with several arms, formed where winds blow from multiple directions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is loess?

options.A: A widespread deposit of wind-blown silt, generally fine-grained and often fertile; the Loess Plateau of China is a classic example
options.B: A deposit of wind-blown sand forming dunes
options.D: A deposit of gravel at the foot of a mountain

questions.explanation: Loess is a widespread deposit of wind-blown silt, generally fine-grained and often fertile. The Loess Plateau of China is a classic example.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between barchan and parabolic dunes?

options.A: Barchan horns point downwind and commonly occur with limited sand and little vegetation; parabolic arms point upwind and are often anchored by vegetation
options.B: Barchan arms point upwind; parabolic horns point downwind
options.C: Barchan dunes are formed by water; parabolic dunes by wind
options.D: Barchan dunes are stabilised by vegetation; parabolic dunes are not

questions.explanation: Barchan horns point downwind and commonly occur with limited sand and little vegetation; parabolic arms point upwind and are often anchored by vegetation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: When does a glacier deposit sediment?

options.A: When ice advances rapidly
options.B: When ice melts, retreats, stagnates or loses its ability to carry debris
options.C: When the glacier is growing and eroding bedrock
options.D: When meltwater freezes at the glacier base

questions.explanation: A glacier deposits sediment when ice melts, retreats, stagnates or loses its ability to carry debris. It releases sediment that may be deposited directly by ice or reworked by meltwater.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is till?

options.A: Stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater
options.B: Unsorted and generally unstratified sediment deposited directly by glacial ice, ranging from clay to large boulders
options.C: A ridge of debris deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier

questions.explanation: Till is unsorted and generally unstratified sediment deposited directly by glacial ice, ranging from clay to large boulders.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a moraine?

options.A: A mound of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater
options.B: An accumulation of glacially transported debris, classified by position and manner of formation
options.C: A long winding ridge of meltwater-deposited sediment
options.D: A broad plain of stratified outwash

questions.explanation: A moraine is an accumulation of glacially transported debris. Moraines are classified by their position and the manner in which they form.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a lateral moraine?

options.A: A ridge of debris deposited along the sides of a glacier
options.B: A debris ridge near the centre of a glacier
options.C: A ridge of debris deposited at the farthest advance of a glacier
options.D: A widespread layer of till deposited beneath the ice

questions.explanation: A lateral moraine is a ridge of debris deposited along the sides of a glacier.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a medial moraine?

options.A: A ridge of debris along the side of a glacier
options.B: A debris ridge near the centre of a glacier, commonly formed where lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join
options.C: A ridge of debris at the farthest advance of a glacier
options.D: A ridge deposited during a temporary pause in glacier retreat

questions.explanation: A medial moraine is a debris ridge near the centre of a glacier, commonly formed where lateral moraines of two tributary glaciers join.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a terminal or end moraine?

options.A: A ridge of debris along the side of a glacier
options.B: A debris ridge near the centre of a glacier
options.C: A ridge of debris deposited at or near the farthest advance of a glacier, marking its maximum extent during that advance
options.D: A widespread layer of till beneath the ice

questions.explanation: A terminal or end moraine is a ridge of debris deposited at or near the farthest advance of a glacier, marking its maximum extent during that advance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a recessional moraine?

options.A: A ridge deposited during a temporary pause or minor readvance as a glacier retreats
options.B: A ridge deposited at the maximum advance of a glacier
options.C: A ridge along the side of a glacier
options.D: A ridge formed where two glaciers join

questions.explanation: A recessional moraine is a ridge deposited during a temporary pause or minor readvance as a glacier retreats.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a ground moraine?

options.A: A ridge of debris at the farthest advance of a glacier
options.B: A widespread, often gently undulating layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice
options.C: A ridge deposited during a pause in glacier retreat
options.D: A ridge along the side of a glacier

questions.explanation: A ground moraine is a widespread, often gently undulating layer of till deposited beneath or left behind by glacier ice.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a drumlin?

options.A: A long winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater
options.B: An elongated, streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment, commonly aligned with former ice flow
options.C: A mound of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater in stagnant ice
options.D: A broad plain of stratified outwash beyond the glacier margin

questions.explanation: A drumlin is an elongated, streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment, commonly aligned with former ice flow. Its precise formation mechanisms are complex and may involve subglacial deposition and deformation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is an esker?

options.A: An elongated streamlined hill of till
options.B: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing within or beneath a glacier
options.C: A mound of stratified sand and gravel deposited in stagnant ice
options.D: A broad plain of stratified outwash

questions.explanation: An esker is a long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing within or beneath a glacier.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a kame?

options.A: A long winding ridge of meltwater-deposited sediment
options.B: A mound or irregular hill of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater in or along stagnant ice; it may remain after the ice melts
options.C: An elongated streamlined hill of till
options.D: A broad plain of stratified outwash

questions.explanation: A kame is a mound or irregular hill of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater in or along stagnant ice; it may remain after the ice melts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is an outwash plain?

options.A: A long winding ridge of meltwater-deposited sediment
options.B: A mound of stratified sand and gravel deposited in stagnant ice
options.C: A broad plain of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams beyond the glacier margin
options.D: A widespread layer of till deposited beneath the ice

questions.explanation: An outwash plain is a broad plain of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams beyond the glacier margin.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How does till differ from outwash?

options.A: Till is deposited directly by ice and is generally unsorted and unstratified; outwash is deposited by meltwater and is usually stratified and better sorted
options.B: Till is deposited by meltwater and is stratified; outwash is deposited directly by ice and is unsorted
options.C: Both are deposited directly by ice and are unsorted
options.D: Both are deposited by meltwater and are well sorted

questions.explanation: Till is deposited directly by ice and is generally unsorted and unstratified; outwash is deposited by meltwater and is usually stratified and better sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: When does marine deposition occur?

options.A: When waves, tides and currents increase in energy
options.B: When waves, tides and currents lose energy or when coastal conditions favour sediment accumulation; sheltered bays, low-energy coasts and river mouths are common settings

questions.explanation: Marine deposition occurs when waves, tides and currents lose energy or when coastal conditions favour sediment accumulation. Sheltered bays, low-energy coasts and river mouths are common depositional settings.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a beach?

options.A: A narrow ridge of sand attached to land at one end
options.B: An accumulation of sand, gravel, pebbles or other sediment along the shore, shaped by waves, tides and currents
options.C: A ridge of sand deposited across a bay
options.D: A shallow body of water separated from the sea by a barrier

questions.explanation: A beach is an accumulation of sand, gravel, pebbles or other sediment along the shore, shaped by waves, tides and currents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a spit?

options.A: A ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay or inlet
options.B: A narrow ridge of sand or shingle attached to land at one end and extending into a bay or estuary, commonly formed by longshore drift
options.C: A ridge of sediment connecting an island to the mainland
options.D: A long narrow coastal deposit lying offshore parallel to the coast

questions.explanation: A spit is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle attached to land at one end and extending into a bay or estuary, commonly formed by longshore drift.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a bar?

options.A: A narrow ridge of sand attached to land at one end
options.B: A ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay or inlet, sometimes joining two headlands and creating a lagoon behind it
options.C: A ridge of sediment connecting an island to the mainland
options.D: A long narrow coastal deposit lying offshore parallel to the coast

questions.explanation: A bar is a ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay or inlet, sometimes joining two headlands and creating a lagoon behind it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a tombolo?

options.A: A narrow ridge of sand attached to land at one end
options.B: A ridge of sand or shingle deposited across a bay
options.C: A ridge or bar of sediment connecting an island to the mainland or to another island
options.D: A shallow body of water separated from the sea by a barrier

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a ridge or bar of sediment connecting an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a barrier beach or barrier island?

options.A: A ridge of sand attached to land at one end
options.B: A long, narrow coastal deposit of sand or shingle lying offshore and roughly parallel to the coast, separated from the mainland by a lagoon or tidal waterway
options.C: A ridge of sediment connecting an island to the mainland
options.D: A shallow body of water separated from the sea by a spit

questions.explanation: A barrier beach or barrier island is a long, narrow coastal deposit of sand or shingle lying offshore and roughly parallel to the coast, separated from the mainland by a lagoon or tidal waterway.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a coastal lagoon?

options.A: A ridge of sand deposited across a bay
options.B: A shallow body of water separated from the sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef, with a restricted connection to the open sea
options.C: A deep narrow glacial valley flooded by seawater
options.D: A crescent-shaped lake formed from a meander

questions.explanation: A coastal lagoon is a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef, with a restricted connection to the open sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is longshore drift?

options.A: The movement of sediment along a coast when waves approach at an angle and swash carries material obliquely up the beach while backwash returns it downslope under gravity
options.B: The movement of sediment directly offshore by backwash
options.C: The deposition of sediment at a river mouth
options.D: The transport of sediment by wind along a beach

questions.explanation: Longshore drift is the movement of sediment along a coast when waves approach at an angle and swash carries material obliquely up the beach while backwash returns it downslope under gravity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: How does a delta differ from a spit?

options.A: A delta forms at a river mouth from river-borne sediment; a spit is a coastal ridge formed mainly by longshore sediment transport and deposition
options.B: A delta is formed by longshore drift; a spit forms at a river mouth
options.C: Both are formed by glacial deposition
options.D: Both are formed by wind deposition

questions.explanation: A delta forms at a river mouth from river-borne sediment; a spit is a coastal ridge formed mainly by longshore sediment transport and deposition.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian region is a classic example of a river depositional feature called a delta?

options.A: Thar Desert, Rajasthan
options.B: Ganga-Brahmaputra delta (Sundarbans)

questions.explanation: The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta (Sundarbans) is a major river depositional feature in India, along with extensive Indo-Gangetic alluvial plains and alluvial fans along Himalayan foothills.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian region is known for extensive wind depositional features such as dunes and aeolian sand deposits?

options.A: Thar Desert, Rajasthan
options.B: Western Ghats

questions.explanation: The Thar Desert in Rajasthan contains extensive dune forms and aeolian sand deposits.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian region is known for glacial erosion and deposition features such as cirques, U-shaped valleys, moraines and glacial lakes?

options.A: Thar Desert
options.B: Himalaya

questions.explanation: The Himalaya is known for glacial erosion and deposition features including cirques, U-shaped valleys, moraines and glacial lakes in high mountain areas.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian coastal region is a classic example of a coastal lagoon system?

options.A: Chilika
options.B: Sundarbans

questions.explanation: Chilika is a coastal lagoon system in India. Beaches, spits, bars and lagoons occur along India's east and west coasts; the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay region includes barrier and shoal features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which Indian region is known for limestone cave systems and karst features?

options.A: Thar Desert
options.B: Meghalaya

questions.explanation: Limestone and cave systems occur in parts of Meghalaya and other carbonate-rock regions; cave development depends on soluble bedrock and groundwater circulation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of river erosion in India?

options.A: Himalayan rivers cut deep valleys and gorges; waterfalls and potholes occur in suitable hard-rock reaches of peninsular rivers
options.B: Thar Desert contains extensive dune forms

questions.explanation: Himalayan rivers cut deep valleys and gorges; waterfalls and potholes occur in suitable hard-rock reaches of peninsular rivers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes erosion, transportation and deposition?

options.A: Erosion is removal; transportation is movement; deposition is settling/accumulation
options.B: Erosion is settling; transportation is removal; deposition is movement
options.C: Erosion is movement; transportation is settling; deposition is removal
options.D: Erosion is accumulation; transportation is removal; deposition is movement

questions.explanation: Erosion is removal; transportation is movement; deposition is settling/accumulation. This is a common exam trap.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes attrition and abrasion?

options.A: Attrition removes loose particles; abrasion wears rock with wind-blown sand
options.B: Attrition means particles collide and become smaller/rounder; abrasion means particles scrape a bedrock or surface
options.C: Attrition is chemical dissolution; abrasion is hydraulic action
options.D: Attrition occurs only in glaciers; abrasion occurs only in rivers

questions.explanation: Attrition means particles collide and become smaller/rounder; abrasion means particles scrape a bedrock or surface.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes deflation and abrasion in wind erosion?

options.A: Deflation wears rock with wind-blown sand; abrasion removes loose particles
options.B: Deflation removes loose particles; abrasion wears rock with wind-blown sand
options.C: Deflation is chemical dissolution; abrasion is hydraulic action
options.D: Deflation occurs only in glaciers; abrasion occurs only in rivers

questions.explanation: Deflation removes loose particles; abrasion wears rock with wind-blown sand.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes glacial plucking and abrasion?

options.A: Plucking scratches and polishes bedrock; abrasion removes blocks
options.B: Plucking removes blocks; abrasion scratches and polishes bedrock
options.C: Plucking is chemical dissolution; abrasion is hydraulic action
options.D: Plucking occurs only in rivers; abrasion occurs only in wind

questions.explanation: Glacial plucking removes blocks; abrasion scratches and polishes bedrock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about till and outwash is correct?

options.A: Till is deposited directly by ice and is generally unsorted; outwash is deposited by meltwater and is stratified/sorted
options.B: Till is deposited by meltwater and is sorted; outwash is deposited directly by ice and is unsorted
options.C: Both till and outwash are deposited directly by ice and are unsorted
options.D: Both till and outwash are deposited by meltwater and are well sorted

questions.explanation: Till is deposited directly by ice and is generally unsorted; outwash is deposited by meltwater and is stratified/sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly classifies glacial landforms?

options.A: Cirque, arête, horn and U-shaped valley are erosional; moraine, esker, kame and outwash plain are depositional
options.B: Cirque, arête, horn and U-shaped valley are depositional; moraine, esker, kame and outwash plain are erosional

questions.explanation: Cirque, arête, horn and U-shaped valley are erosional glacial landforms; moraine, esker, kame and outwash plain are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly classifies desert landforms?

options.A: Yardangs and ventifacts are depositional; dunes and loess are erosional
options.B: Yardangs and ventifacts are erosional; dunes and loess are depositional

questions.explanation: Yardangs and ventifacts are erosional; dunes and loess are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: On which part of a meander do point bars form and on which part are cut banks found?

options.A: Point bars form on outer bends; cut banks are on inner bends
options.B: Point bars form on inner meander bends; cut banks are erosional on outer bends
options.C: Both point bars and cut banks form on inner bends
options.D: Both point bars and cut banks form on outer bends

questions.explanation: River point bars form on inner meander bends; cut banks are erosional on outer bends.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly classifies coastal landforms?

options.A: Spits and tombolos are erosional; caves, arches, stacks and wave-cut platforms are depositional
options.B: Spits and tombolos are depositional; caves, arches, stacks and wave-cut platforms are erosional

questions.explanation: Spits and tombolos are coastal depositional features; caves, arches, stacks and wave-cut platforms are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Stalactites and stalagmites are examples of which type of feature?

options.A: Erosional features formed by groundwater dissolution
options.B: Cave deposition features, even though caves themselves are commonly formed by groundwater erosion

questions.explanation: Stalactites and stalagmites are cave deposition features, even though caves themselves are commonly formed by groundwater erosion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about delta formation is correct?

options.A: Delta formation is automatic at every river mouth
options.B: Delta formation is not automatic at every river mouth; waves, tides and currents can remove or redistribute sediment
options.C: Deltas form only where rivers have no sediment load
options.D: Deltas form only in glacial environments

questions.explanation: Delta formation is not automatic at every river mouth; waves, tides and currents can remove or redistribute sediment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists river erosion processes?

options.A: Deflation, abrasion and attrition
options.B: Hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution
options.D: Hydraulic action and abrasion by waves

questions.explanation: River erosion processes are hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists wind erosion processes?

options.A: Hydraulic action and solution
options.B: Plucking and abrasion

questions.explanation: Wind erosion processes are deflation and abrasion. Wind transport modes are suspension, saltation and surface creep.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists glacial erosion processes?

options.A: Deflation and attrition
options.B: Hydraulic action and solution

questions.explanation: Glacial erosion processes are plucking and abrasion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists marine erosion processes?

options.A: Plucking and abrasion
options.B: Deflation and attrition
options.C: Hydraulic action and abrasion by waves

questions.explanation: Marine erosion processes are hydraulic action and abrasion by waves.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes groundwater erosion?

options.A: Deflation of loose particles
options.B: Dissolution of soluble rocks; karst topography

questions.explanation: Groundwater erosion is the dissolution of soluble rocks, producing karst topography.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists river transport modes?

options.A: Traction, saltation, suspension, solution
options.B: Deflation, abrasion, attrition

questions.explanation: River transport modes are traction, saltation, suspension and solution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about glacial till and outwash is correct?

options.A: Glacial till = sorted; meltwater outwash = unsorted
options.B: Glacial till = unsorted; meltwater outwash = stratified and better sorted
options.D: Both are stratified and well sorted

questions.explanation: Glacial till is unsorted; meltwater outwash is stratified and better sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about dune horns and arms is correct?

options.A: Barchan horns point upwind; parabolic dune arms point downwind
options.B: Barchan horns point downwind; parabolic dune arms point upwind
options.C: Both barchan horns and parabolic arms point downwind
options.D: Both barchan horns and parabolic arms point upwind

questions.explanation: Barchan horns point downwind; parabolic dune arms point upwind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which statement about spits and tombolos is correct?

options.A: A spit is attached at one end; a tombolo connects an island to land
options.B: A spit connects an island to land; a tombolo is attached at one end
options.C: Both are attached at both ends

questions.explanation: A spit is attached at one end; a tombolo connects an island to land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: When does deposition occur?

options.A: When carrying capacity or transporting energy increases
options.B: When carrying capacity or transporting energy decreases
options.C: When the transporting agent speeds up
options.D: When sediment load decreases below capacity

questions.explanation: Deposition occurs when carrying capacity or transporting energy decreases.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Erosion differs from weathering because erosion involves:

options.A: Only chemical change
options.B: Removal and transport

questions.explanation: Erosion removes material from its original location. Weathering breaks down or alters rock in place.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which is NOT a principal river erosion process?

options.A: Hydraulic action
options.B: Abrasion

questions.explanation: Sublimation is a phase change, not a standard river erosion process.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Removal of loose particles by wind is called:

options.A: Deflation
options.B: Plucking

questions.explanation: Deflation is wind removal of loose material.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A U-shaped valley is mainly formed by:

options.A: River deposition
options.B: Glacial erosion

questions.explanation: A valley glacier widens and deepens a pre-existing valley, forming a U-shaped valley.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial process removes blocks of bedrock?

options.A: Plucking
options.B: Saltation

questions.explanation: Plucking/quarrying detaches blocks from bedrock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A spit is formed mainly by:

options.A: Groundwater solution
options.B: Longshore drift

questions.explanation: Longshore drift transports and deposits sediment along the coast, forming a spit.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which is a depositional glacial landform?

options.A: Cirque
options.B: Arête

questions.explanation: An esker is a ridge of meltwater-deposited stratified sediment and is depositional. Cirque, arête and horn are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sediment transport mode involves hopping or bouncing?

options.A: Suspension
options.B: Saltation

questions.explanation: Saltation is a series of short leaps or hops.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Till is generally:

options.A: Well-sorted and stratified
options.B: Directly deposited by ice and poorly sorted

questions.explanation: Till contains a wide range of particle sizes deposited by ice and is generally poorly sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which is an erosional coastal landform?

options.A: Tombolo
options.B: Spit

questions.explanation: Wave action cuts a platform as cliffs retreat. Tombolo, spit and beach are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A crescent-shaped dune with horns pointing downwind is:

options.A: Parabolic
options.B: Barchan

questions.explanation: Barchan horns point downwind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A parabolic dune commonly has arms pointing:

options.A: Downwind
options.B: Upwind

questions.explanation: Vegetation anchors the arms, which point upwind.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A delta forms mainly where:

options.A: A river enters standing water and deposits sediment
options.B: A glacier plucks bedrock

questions.explanation: The river loses velocity and deposits sediment at its mouth where it enters standing water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which is a groundwater solution landform?

options.A: Yardang
options.B: Sinkhole

questions.explanation: Sinkholes are characteristic of karst terrain formed by groundwater solution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: A natural levee forms due to:

options.A: Wind abrasion
options.B: Overbank river deposition

questions.explanation: Floodwater deposits coarser sediment near channel banks, forming a natural levee.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are interlocking spurs?

options.A: Depositional features on the inner bends of meanders
options.B: Erosional landforms in the upper course where alternate valley sides project into the valley, interlocking with each other
options.C: Ridges of glacial debris along valley sides

questions.explanation: Interlocking spurs are landforms produced by river erosion, common in the upper course where the river winds around alternating projections of valley sides.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are incised meanders?

options.A: Meanders formed by deposition in a floodplain
options.B: Meanders that have been cut deeply into bedrock by renewed vertical erosion

questions.explanation: Incised meanders are a river erosion landform where meanders are deeply cut into bedrock, often due to rejuvenation or uplift.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a river cliff or cut bank?

options.A: A depositional feature on the inner bend of a meander
options.B: A steep bank formed by lateral erosion on the outer bend of a meander
options.C: A ridge of debris along a glacier
options.D: A cliff formed by wave action

questions.explanation: River cliffs or cut banks are erosional features on the outer bends of meanders where lateral erosion is strongest. Point bars form on the inner bends.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What are rapids?

options.A: Sections of a river where the gradient is steep and the water flows quickly over resistant rocks or boulders
options.B: Depositional features at a river mouth

questions.explanation: Rapids are sections of a river with steep gradient and turbulent flow over resistant rocks or boulders, and are a river erosion landform.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea cave?

options.A: A vertical opening connected to a sea cave through which air and water are forced upwards
options.B: A hollow eroded into a cliff by wave action, especially where waves enlarge weaknesses and joints
options.C: A narrow steep-sided inlet cut into a rocky coast
options.D: A gently sloping rocky platform left by cliff retreat

questions.explanation: A sea cave is a hollow eroded into a cliff by wave action where waves enlarge weaknesses and joints. It may later cut through a headland to form an arch.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea arch?

options.A: A cave that has cut through a headland, leaving a bridge of rock with an opening beneath
options.B: A vertical opening connected to a sea cave
options.C: A narrow steep-sided inlet cut into a rocky coast

questions.explanation: A sea arch forms when a cave cuts through a headland. Collapse of the arch roof may leave a stack.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea stack?

options.A: A cave that has cut through a headland
options.B: An isolated pillar of rock left standing offshore after the collapse of a sea arch
options.C: A narrow steep-sided inlet cut into a rocky coast

questions.explanation: A sea stack is an isolated pillar of rock left offshore after the collapse of a sea arch. Continued erosion and collapse reduce it to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is a sea stump?

options.A: An isolated pillar of rock offshore
options.B: The remnant of a sea stack after continued erosion and collapse, often submerged at high tide
options.C: A cave cutting through a headland

questions.explanation: A sea stump is the remnant of a sea stack after continued erosion and collapse. It is often submerged at high tide.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an erosional desert landform?

options.A: Barchan dune
options.B: Loess deposit

questions.explanation: Yardangs are erosional desert landforms carved by wind abrasion and deflation. Barchan dunes, transverse dunes and loess are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an erosional glacial landform?

options.A: Esker
options.B: Kame

questions.explanation: A cirque is an erosional glacial landform. Esker, kame and outwash plain are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional glacial landform?

options.A: Arête
options.B: Horn

questions.explanation: A drumlin is an elongated hill of glacial sediment and is depositional. Arête, horn and U-shaped valley are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional coastal landform?

options.A: Sea cave
options.B: Sea arch

questions.explanation: A spit is a depositional coastal landform formed by longshore drift. Sea cave, sea arch and wave-cut notch are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a groundwater erosion landform?

options.A: Barchan dune
options.B: Sinkhole

questions.explanation: Sinkholes are karst landforms formed by groundwater solution. Barchan dune is wind depositional, esker is glacial depositional, and spit is marine depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a form of solution/corrosion?

options.A: The force of water pressure loosening material
options.B: Chemical dissolution of soluble rock by water

questions.explanation: Solution or corrosion is the chemical dissolution of soluble minerals and rocks by water, especially weakly acidic water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which process deepens a plunge pool at the base of a waterfall?

options.A: Deflation
options.B: Hydraulic action and abrasion

questions.explanation: Hydraulic action and abrasion deepen a plunge pool and undercut the resistant ledge at a waterfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial landform is formed when several cirques erode back towards one another?

options.A: Arête
options.B: Horn

questions.explanation: A horn is a sharp, pyramidal mountain peak formed when several cirques erode back towards one another. An arête forms between adjacent cirques or glacially eroded valleys.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Why may waterfalls occur at the outlet of a hanging valley?

options.A: Because the hanging valley is at a lower level than the main trough
options.B: Because the hanging valley is left at a higher level than the main glacial trough, and water drops down to the main valley
options.C: Because the hanging valley is formed by wind erosion
options.D: Because the hanging valley is a depositional feature

questions.explanation: A hanging valley is a tributary glacial valley left at a higher level than the main glacial trough because the main glacier eroded more deeply. Waterfalls may occur at its outlet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is an important form of hydraulic action on a coast?

options.A: Wave quarrying and pressure in joints
options.B: Deflation and abrasion

questions.explanation: Wave quarrying and pressure in joints are important forms of hydraulic action in marine erosion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which acid is formed when rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and soil?

options.A: Sulphuric acid
options.B: Carbonic acid

questions.explanation: Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and soil, forming weak carbonic acid, which dissolves calcite in limestone.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following deposits is typically well-sorted?

options.A: Glacial till
options.B: Wind-blown sand

questions.explanation: Wind and waves often produce well-sorted deposits. Glacial till is typically poorly sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following deposits is typically poorly sorted?

options.A: Wind-blown sand
options.B: Wave-deposited beach sand

questions.explanation: Glacial till is typically poorly sorted because it is deposited directly by ice without the sorting action of water or wind. Outwash is stratified and better sorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Where is deposition common in a river system?

options.A: On outer meander bends and steep upper courses
options.B: On inner meander bends, floodplains, river mouths and where gradient decreases

questions.explanation: River deposition is common on inner meander bends, floodplains, river mouths and where gradient decreases.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What controls delta development at a river mouth?

options.A: Only the river's length
options.B: Sediment supply, waves, tides and currents

questions.explanation: Delta development depends on sediment supply, waves, tides and currents. Delta formation is not automatic at every river mouth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the classic example of a loess deposit?

options.A: Sahara Desert
options.B: Loess Plateau of China

questions.explanation: The Loess Plateau of China is a classic example of loess, a widespread deposit of wind-blown silt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which glacial deposit is stratified and better sorted?

options.A: Till
options.B: Ground moraine

questions.explanation: Outwash is deposited by meltwater and is usually stratified and better sorted, unlike till which is deposited directly by ice and is unsorted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the main process responsible for the formation of a spit?

options.A: Glacial plucking
options.B: Longshore drift

questions.explanation: A spit is commonly formed by longshore drift, which transports sediment along the coast and deposits it where the coastline changes direction or the flow energy decreases.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following connects an island to the mainland or to another island?

options.A: Spit
options.B: Bar

questions.explanation: A tombolo is a ridge or bar of sediment connecting an island to the mainland or to another island.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef?

options.A: Fjord
options.B: Coastal lagoon

questions.explanation: A coastal lagoon is a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a spit, bar, barrier island or reef, with a restricted connection to the open sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following rocks are commonly associated with karst landscapes?

options.A: Granite and basalt
options.B: Limestone, dolomite and gypsum

questions.explanation: Karst landscapes develop mainly by solution of soluble rocks such as limestone, dolomite or gypsum.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the main difference between a waterfall and rapids?

options.A: A waterfall is a vertical drop; rapids are turbulent, fast-flowing sections over resistant rocks or boulders without a single vertical drop
options.B: A waterfall is formed by wind; rapids by water
options.C: A waterfall is depositional; rapids are erosional
options.D: A waterfall forms in the lower course; rapids form in the upper course

questions.explanation: A waterfall involves a vertical drop where differential erosion creates a step. Rapids are turbulent, fast-flowing sections over resistant rocks or boulders, without necessarily a single vertical drop.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the difference between a drumlin and an esker?

options.A: A drumlin is a winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel; an esker is an elongated hill of till
options.B: A drumlin is an elongated streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment; an esker is a long winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater
options.D: Both are formed by wind deposition

questions.explanation: A drumlin is an elongated, streamlined hill composed mainly of glacial sediment. An esker is a long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which dune type forms where winds blow from multiple directions?

options.A: Barchan
options.B: Parabolic

questions.explanation: A star dune is a high, pyramidal dune with several arms, formed where winds blow from multiple directions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Arrange the coastal erosional features in the correct sequence of formation from a cave.

options.A: Cave → stack → arch → stump
options.B: Cave → arch → stack → stump

questions.explanation: Waves enlarge weaknesses and joints to form caves. A cave may cut through a headland to form an arch. Collapse of the arch roof leaves a stack; continued erosion and collapse reduce it to a stump.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between an alluvial fan and a delta?

options.A: An alluvial fan forms where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain; a delta forms at a river mouth where the river enters standing water
options.B: An alluvial fan forms at a river mouth; a delta forms at the foot of a mountain
options.C: Both form only in glacial environments

questions.explanation: An alluvial fan is a fan-shaped deposit formed where a stream emerges from a steep mountain valley onto a flatter plain. A delta is a depositional landform at a river mouth where sediment accumulates as the river enters standing water.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What is the difference between a deflation hollow and a desert pavement?

options.A: A deflation hollow is a depression formed by wind removing loose material; a desert pavement is a surface layer of closely packed pebbles left behind after wind removes finer particles
options.B: A deflation hollow is a surface layer of pebbles; a desert pavement is a depression
options.D: Both are formed by glacial action

questions.explanation: A deflation hollow or blowout is a depression formed when wind removes loose surface material. A desert pavement is a surface layer of closely packed pebbles and gravel left behind after wind removes finer particles by deflation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a glacial erosional landform?

options.A: Cirque
options.B: Arête

questions.explanation: A drumlin is a depositional glacial landform composed mainly of glacial sediment. Cirque, arête and hanging valley are erosional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a depositional feature in karst landscapes?

options.A: Sinkhole
options.B: Swallow hole

questions.explanation: Stalactites (and stalagmites) are depositional cave formations produced by precipitation of calcite from solution. Sinkholes, swallow holes and dolines are erosional or collapse features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a landform produced by river erosion?

options.A: Point bar
options.B: Natural levee

questions.explanation: Incised meanders are a river erosion landform. Point bars, natural levees and alluvial fans are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
